frontMatter.introduction:
ISRPL has established a comprehensive, integrated, and structured management framework to ensure standardization, operational excellence, regulatory compliance, and continuous improvement across all business functions.

This Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) is developed to provide a formalized, consistent, and controlled approach for managing specific processes in alignment with ISRPL's strategic objectives and sustainability commitments.

The key objectives of this SOP are to:
Establish a clear, systematic, and standardized methodology for execution of the defined process
Ensure compliance with all applicable legal, statutory, regulatory, and internal policy requirements
Enhance operational efficiency, process reliability, and quality of outcomes
Strengthen risk identification, mitigation, and control mechanisms
Promote accountability and clarity in roles and responsibilities across functions
Enable effective monitoring, measurement, and performance evaluation
Support data integrity, documentation control, and traceability of records
Integrate Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) principles, including:
Resource efficiency
Environmental protection
Occupational health and safety
Ethical and responsible business practices
Foster a culture of continuous improvement, innovation, and employee engagement

This SOP also ensures that all activities are carried out in a manner that aligns with ISRPL's commitment to sustainable development, stakeholder trust, and long-term value creation.

frontMatter.reviewMechanism:
This SOP has been duly reviewed and formally approved by the Top Management of ISRPL, confirming that the procedures outlined herein are accurate, relevant, and aligned with the organization's operational, regulatory, and ESG requirements.

All departments and employees are expected to comply with the provisions of this SOP. Any changes, deviations, or revisions shall be undertaken only with prior approval from the authorized authorities and in accordance with the established review process. This SOP shall become effective from the date of approval and will remain in force until it is revised or superseded through the formal document control mechanism.

sops.title: Energy Consumption Reduction and GHG Emissions Management

blocks.text:
ISRPL has implemented a comprehensive, data-driven energy and greenhouse gas (GHG) management framework aimed at systematically reducing energy consumption, improving operational efficiency, and minimizing emissions across all business activities.

The organization has formally committed to achieving Net Zero emissions by 2050, supported by a structured decarbonization roadmap, defined baseline emissions, and a continuously monitored Carbon Reduction Action Tracker.

ISRPL has established FY 2022–23 as its baseline year, which serves as the reference point for measuring progress in emission reduction. This baseline enables identification of emission hotspots, prioritization of reduction initiatives, and tracking of performance improvements over time.

This SOP applies to all ISRPL operations, including:

Manufacturing processes and production lines
Utility systems (boilers, cooling towers, compressors, DG sets, etc.)
Administrative and support functions
Logistics, transportation, and supply chain activities
It covers all energy sources (electricity, fuels, thermal energy) and emissions categories:

Scope 1: Direct emissions from fuel combustion and operations
Scope 2: Indirect emissions from purchased electricity
Scope 3: Indirect emissions from supply chain, logistics, and business activities

blocks.text: ISRPL has established a cross-functional governance structure to ensure effective implementation and monitoring:

ISRPL has implemented a comprehensive portfolio of energy and carbon reduction initiatives, which are tracked through a centralized Carbon Reduction Action Tracker capturing initiative details, timelines, responsibilities, and status (completed / ongoing / planned).

steps.heading: Technology Modernization and Energy Efficiency Enhancement

body.text:
ISRPL has implemented extensive technology upgrades to improve energy efficiency.

Key initiatives include:

100% LED lighting replacement (completed)
Installation of motion sensor-based lighting systems (in progress)
Deployment of smart energy meters for real-time monitoring (planned for full coverage)
Replacement and upgrade of energy-efficient pumps and equipment
Implementation of Leak Detection and Repair (LDAR) program (quarterly ongoing)
Retrofitting of DG sets to reduce NOx and SOx emissions (completed)
Performance approach:

Continuous monitoring of equipment efficiency
Preventive and predictive maintenance practices

steps.heading: Capacity Building and Employee Engagement on Energy & Climate Action

body.text:
ISRPL has embedded a strong culture of sustainability through continuous employee engagement and awareness programs.

Implemented practices include:

Structured training programs on energy conservation, climate change, and GHG reduction
Inclusion of sustainability modules in employee induction and refresher training
Awareness campaigns on Net Zero commitment and responsible energy use
Behavioural initiatives such as:
Promotion of carpooling and shared transportation (ongoing)
Encouragement of virtual meetings to reduce business travel
Integration of sustainability responsibilities into employee roles and performance expectations
Impact:

Improved employee participation in energy-saving practices
Increased awareness of carbon footprint and reduction measures

steps.heading: Structured Energy and Carbon Performance Assessments

body.text:
ISRPL conducts structured energy and carbon audits to identify inefficiencies and drive continuous improvement.

Implemented practices include:

Internal and third-party energy audits
Identification of inefficiencies, losses, and emission-intensive processes
Development of corrective action plans tracked through the Carbon Reduction Action Tracker
Baseline Emissions (FY 2022–23):

Scope 1: 1,361.68 tCO₂eq
Scope 2: 42,429.29 tCO₂eq
Scope 3: 145,881.56 tCO₂eq
Total: 189,672.54 tCO₂eq
Insight:
Majority emissions from Scope 3, guiding supply chain-focused strategies
Follow-up mechanism:

Tracking of audit recommendations through action registers
Periodic review meetings to monitor closure of identified actions
Documentation of achieved energy savings and emission reductions

ISRPL has taken significant steps to decarbonize its energy mix through renewable energy adoption.

Implemented actions include:

Commissioning of a 2.7 MWp on-site solar power plant, contributing to reduction in Scope 2 emissions
Planned expansion through additional 0.5 MWp solar installation
Exploration of long-term green energy sourcing agreements
Continuous evaluation of additional renewable energy opportunities across locations
Management approach:

Monthly monitoring of renewable energy generation and consumption
Tracking renewable energy contribution as a percentage of total energy mix

steps.heading: Waste Heat Recovery and Energy Efficiency Enhancement Initiatives

body.text:
ISRPL has implemented systems to improve thermal energy efficiency and reduce fuel consumption.

Implemented practices include:

Installation of waste heat recovery systems in process areas
Reuse of recovered heat for process heating and utility applications
Evaluation and planning of back-pressure turbine installation (target: 2029)
Utilization of recovered heat for:
Preheating of feed materials
Steam generation or other thermal requirements
Deployment of Combined Heat and Power (CHP) systems where feasible to generate electricity and useful heat simultaneously
Performance management:

Continuous monitoring of heat recovery efficiency
Periodic maintenance to ensure optimal system performance
Measurement and documentation of energy savings achieved

ISRPL has implemented fuel transition strategies to reduce reliance on high-carbon fuels and improve overall energy efficiency.

Key actions include:

Replacement of conventional fuels such as coal and furnace oil with cleaner alternatives like natural gas
Transition from conventional fuels to RLNG (Regasified Liquefied Natural Gas) in production processes
Optimization of combustion systems to improve efficiency
Evaluation and adoption of low-carbon or alternative fuels where technically feasible
Continuous monitoring of fuel consumption patterns and emission factors
Impact tracking:

Reduction in Scope 1 emissions intensity
Measurement of reduction in emission intensity due to fuel switch
Periodic reporting and review of fuel efficiency improvements

ISRPL has implemented initiatives to reduce emissions from logistics and transportation.

Key actions include:

Adoption of multimodal transport systems (90–95% implemented)
Transition to electric material handling:
9 out of 14 forklifts battery-operated
Remaining fleet planned for electrification by 2025
Evaluation of fuel-efficient and alternative fuel vehicles

steps.heading: Supply Chain and Scope 3 Emission Reduction Initiatives

body.text:
ISRPL actively manages Scope 3 emissions through supplier engagement.

Practices include:

Communication of GHG reduction requirements to suppliers
Supplier acknowledgment and implementation of emission reduction practices

steps.heading: Waste Reduction through Reuse, Recovery and Repurposing

body.text: ISRPL has implemented a structured waste minimization strategy by integrating material recovery, reuse, and repurposing practices within operations.
Enhanced practices with plant-level implementation:

Recovery of usable materials through distillation, filtration, and neutralization systems
Reuse of recovered materials in production after QA/QC validation
Disposal of waste rubber to authorized vendors for reprocessing
Utilization of centrifuge sludge as manure for agricultural purposes
Conversion of waste streams into value-added outputs through:
Waste-to-compost initiatives
Bio-remediation trials
Process-level reuse example:
Unusable styrene is routed to liquid waste incinerator, generating steam for process reuse, ensuring energy recovery and waste minimization
Impact:

Reduction in internal waste generation
Improved circular economy performance
Resource and energy efficiency enhancement

body.text: ISRPL has implemented a comprehensive waste segregation and disposal system, aligned with waste classification and regulatory requirements.

Solid Waste Handling and Disposal

Office waste segregated into:
Green bins (biodegradable)
Red bins (non-biodegradable)

Stored in 500 kg jumbo bags

Reused as manure for agricultural applications
Metal scrap:
Collected in drums and sold to authorized recyclers
Waste rubber:
Sent to vendors for reprocessing

Stored under controlled conditions (water sprinkling)
Sent for incineration

Wastewater (~3000 m³/day) treated in WWTP through:
Biological oxidation
Filtration
Reverse osmosis
Treated water reused for:
Cooling tower makeup
Gardening
Used oil:
Collected in barrels
Sent to authorized recyclers
Gaseous Waste Handling

Exhaust gases treated in scrubber systems before release
Continuous monitoring through online analyzers
Vent gases routed to flare system for complete combustion
Storage & Handling Controls:

Use of designated containers (bins, drums, jumbo bags)
Clear labelling and segregation
Prevention of mixing incompatible waste

ISRPL has demonstrated a structured approach to replacing hazardous substances with safer alternatives through technical evaluation and trials.
Case Implementation: Replacement of TNPP with Safer Antioxidant (A6)

TNPP (existing antioxidant) was identified under REACH SVHC compliance list, prompting substitution
ISRPL introduced A6 antioxidant (C25H44OS2) as a safer alternative
Structured evaluation approach:

Laboratory trials conducted as per SOP and standard ASTM methods
Comparative analysis performed on:
Visual appearance (before and after ageing)
Mooney viscosity
Physical properties (tensile strength, modulus, elongation)
Key results:

Performance of A6 found comparable to TNPP
No significant deviation observed in polymer properties
Product quality maintained within ISRPL specifications
Conclusion and implementation:

Safer antioxidant successfully validated
Recommended for plant-scale implementation
Impact:

Reduction in use of hazardous (SVHC-listed) substances
Compliance with international regulatory standards
Improved environmental and product safety profile

The cooling tower system forms a critical component of water consumption, and ISRPL has established detailed operational and treatment controls to ensure efficient and responsible water usage.

steps.heading: Groundwater Protection and Contamination Prevention Systems

body.text: ISRPL has implemented preventive and control measures to eliminate risks of groundwater contamination.
Preventive infrastructure:

Impervious flooring and bunding in chemical storage and handling areas
Dedicated drainage systems segregating stormwater and effluent
Leak-proof pipelines and storage systems
Operational controls:

Spill prevention and emergency response procedures
Regular inspection of tanks, pipelines, and storage areas
Hazardous material handling protocols

steps.heading: Comprehensive Water Auditing and Loss Reduction Program

body.text: ISRPL has implemented a structured and periodic water auditing mechanism to identify inefficiencies and drive reduction initiatives.
Audit approach

Detailed mapping of water flow across:
Process consumption
Cooling and boiler systems
Domestic and auxiliary usage
Identification of:
High consumption zones
Leakages and unaccounted losses
Inefficient practices or equipment
Implementation controls

Installation of digital water meters and submeters across critical points
Development of water balance diagrams for each facility
Benchmarking water consumption per unit of production
Corrective actions

Leak detection and rectification programs
Optimization of process water usage
Standardization of operating procedures to reduce wastage

steps.heading: Water-Efficient Cooling and Utility Management Systems

body.text: Cooling systems are one of the highest water-consuming utilities; ISRPL has optimized them through efficiency measures.
Implemented initiatives

Operation of cooling towers at optimized cycles of concentration (CoC) to reduce blowdown losses
Use of recycled treated water in cooling systems
Installation of automatic chemical dosing systems to maintain water quality and reduce scaling
Use of drift eliminators to minimize evaporative losses
Operational controls

Continuous monitoring of:
Blowdown quantity
Make-up water requirement
Cooling efficiency parameters
Periodic descaling and maintenance to sustain performance

steps.heading: Advanced Water Recycling and Circular Water Use Systems

body.text: ISRPL has implemented a multi-stage water recycling and reuse system to significantly reduce dependence on freshwater sources.
System infrastructure and practices:

Installation of Effluent Treatment Plants (ETP) for industrial wastewater and Sewage Treatment Plants (STP) for domestic wastewater
Use of primary, secondary, and tertiary treatment processes, including filtration and biological treatment
Deployment of tertiary polishing units (e.g., RO / UF where applicable) to enhance reuse quality
Segregation of high-load and low-load effluent streams to optimize treatment efficiency
Water reuse integration:

Treated water is actively reused in:
Cooling tower make-up
Boiler feed (after appropriate treatment)
Utility washing and floor cleaning
Greenbelt and landscaping
Implementation of closed-loop circulation systems in utilities to minimize discharge
Control & monitoring:

Flow meters installed at key inlet, outlet, and reuse points
Daily water balance analysis (input vs reuse vs discharge)
Targets defined for increasing reuse percentage

steps.heading: Site-Level Water Risk Assessment and Mitigation Planning

body.text: ISRPL conducts comprehensive water risk assessments to evaluate both operational and geographical risks.
Risk identification includes:

Water scarcity and dependency on external sources
Impact on local water tables and surrounding communities
Regulatory risks related to water withdrawal and discharge
Climate-related risks (rainfall variability, drought conditions)
Mitigation measures implemented:

Reduction of freshwater dependency through reuse systems
Development of contingency plans for water shortages
Prioritization of critical operations during water stress scenarios

body.text: ISRPL operates an open recirculating cooling water system designed to optimize water use and minimize freshwater consumption through efficient heat exchange and controlled evaporation.
System configuration includes

Cooling tower with 3 cells
Circulation rate: 5000 m³/hr
Holding volume: 1975 m³
Cycle of concentration maintained at ~6 cycles
Evaporation loss: 53.1 m³/hr
Controlled blowdown: 10.71 m³/hr
Operational practices implemented

Operation of pumps based on plant load to avoid excess water usage
Maintaining discharge and return pressures within defined limits
Optimized use of cooling tower cells and fans as per process requirement
Continuous monitoring of supply and return temperatures

Scale inhibitors
Corrosion inhibitors
Bio-dispersants

steps.heading: Zero Liquid Discharge (ZLD) System and Water Monitoring Framework

body.text: ISRPL has implemented a Zero Liquid Discharge (ZLD) system to ensure complete recycling and reuse of wastewater, eliminating any liquid discharge outside the facility.
System configuration and operation:

Industrial wastewater generated from manufacturing operations is treated through Effluent Treatment Plant (ETP) and Reverse Osmosis (RO) systems
The RO reject is further processed in a Multiple Effect Evaporator (MEE) system
Recovered water is reused across operations, including:
Process operations
Cooling systems
Utility applications such as gardening
Residue management: The remaining solid residue in the form of salts is safely handled and disposed of through authorized vendors in compliance with regulatory requirements
Water monitoring and measurement: Water consumption is mapped across key operational areas, including:

Polymerization processes
Cooling systems
Finishing operations
Flow meters are installed at major consumption points to enable section-wise monitoring. Water consumption data is recorded and reviewed on a monthly basis.
Performance tracking:

Water intensity is calculated as cubic meters (m³) per metric ton (MT) of production
This metric is used as a key performance indicator (KPI) to assess water efficiency and drive optimization
Estimation and data reliability:

In areas where direct measurement is not feasible, water consumption is estimated using operational data and water balance analysis
Steam required for operations is sourced externally via pipeline supply; therefore, boiler water consumption is not considered within the site boundary
Impact:

Achievement of zero wastewater discharge
Maximized water reuse and reduced freshwater dependency
Strengthened regulatory compliance and environmental protection

steps.heading: Product Environmental Impact Assessment and Technical Studies

body.text: ISRPL conducts structured technical and environmental studies to evaluate the impact of product formulations and identify opportunities for improvement.
Implemented Case Study: Replacement of Hazardous Antioxidant (TNPP → A6)

ISRPL identified that TNPP (Tris Nonylphenyl Phosphite), used as an antioxidant in SBR1502 rubber, was included in the REACH SVHC (Substances of Very High Concern) list, posing environmental and regulatory risks.
Action Taken:
Initiated a detailed technical and environmental performance study to replace TNPP with a safer alternative antioxidant (A6 / C25H44OS2)
Study Methodology:

Laboratory trials conducted as per ISRPL SOP and international standards
Comparative analysis between TNPP and A6 based on:
Visual appearance before and after ageing
Thermal ageing performance (140°C / 1 hour)
Mooney viscosity (ASTM D1646)
Mechanical properties (ASTM D412)
Oxidation stability under controlled conditions
Key Observations:

Comparable product appearance before and after ageing
Negligible difference in Mooney viscosity (performance consistency maintained)
Mechanical and physical properties remained within specification limits
No adverse impact on product quality or process performance
Outcome:

A6 antioxidant validated as a technically equivalent and environmentally safer substitute
Recommended for plant-scale implementation
Environmental Impact:

Elimination/reduction of SVHC-listed chemical usage
Improved product environmental compliance
Reduced risk of hazardous discharge during product lifecycle

blocks.text: ISRPL has implemented a comprehensive and technically robust framework for the prevention, control, monitoring, and continuous reduction of air emissions, noise, and other environmental nuisances arising from its operations.

The objective is to minimize emissions at source, deploy effective pollution control technologies, and ensure continuous compliance with regulatory standards, while aligning with the organization’s broader sustainability and decarbonization commitments.

The approach integrates process optimization, cleaner fuel transition (RLNG), advanced control systems, structured monitoring, and preventive maintenance practices to manage particulate matter, gaseous pollutants (SO₂, NOx, VOCs), fugitive emissions, noise, and odor.

Process units and production lines

steps.heading: Gaseous Emission Control (VOC, SO₂, NOx, Odor Control Systems)

body.text: ISRPL has implemented advanced exhaust gas treatment systems to control gaseous emissions and odor from process operations.
Exhaust Gas Scrubber System (Implemented and Operational)
ISRPL operates an Exhaust Gas Scrubber system to treat process emissions, particularly from dryer operations, ensuring removal of water-soluble pollutants and odor-causing compounds.
Working Principle:

Exhaust gases are routed to the scrubber system
Water acts as the primary absorbent medium
NaOH (caustic solution) is dosed to neutralize acidic gases
Pollutants are absorbed into the liquid phase, reducing emission load
Operational Controls and Practices:

Maintenance of scrubber water level between 50–55% for optimal absorption
Continuous water circulation using dedicated pumps
Controlled dosing of caustic solution to maintain pH between 9–9.5
Proper gas line alignment from process units to scrubber system
Monitoring of system performance through:
pH levels
Flow conditions
Gas absorption efficiency
Maintenance and Performance Optimization:

Periodic acid wash (every 15 days or based on pressure drop) to remove accumulated contaminants from packing
Monitoring of differential pressure across scrubber
Turbidity-based cleaning validation
Troubleshooting practices for:
Odor issues (water saturation)
pH imbalance (caustic flow issues)
Flow measurement inaccuracies
Environmental Impact:

Effective removal of acidic gases and soluble pollutants
Significant reduction in odor emissions
Improved ambient air quality and regulatory compliance

sops.title: Incident Response Plan (IRP) for Breaches of Confidential Information

blocks.text: ISRPL has established a structured Incident Response Plan (IRP) to identify, manage, and mitigate breaches of confidential information, ensuring timely response, minimal impact, and compliance with legal and organizational requirements.
The objectives of this SOP are to:

Ensure rapid detection and response to data breaches
Minimize damage to business operations, reputation, and stakeholders
Protect confidential, personal, and proprietary information
Establish clear roles, responsibilities, and escalation mechanisms
Ensure proper documentation, reporting, and corrective actions

responsibilities: Detects, investigates, and contains digital security incidents
Implements technical controls and recovery measures
Assesses regulatory implications
Handles legal reporting and compliance requirements
Manages employee-related breaches and disciplinary actions
Conducts awareness and training programs
Ensure reporting of incidents within their teams
Support investigation and corrective actions
Cross-functional team responsible for managing incidents end-to-end
Immediately report any suspected or actual data breach

blocks.text: ISRPL follows a structured and time-bound response process:

body.text: Incidents may be identified through:

System alerts and security monitoring tools
Unauthorized access attempts or login anomalies
Loss or theft of devices or documents
Suspicious emails or phishing attempts
Employee or third-party reporting
Immediate action:

Any employee identifying a breach must report immediately to:
Reporting Manager
IT Department / HSE
Once reported, the incident is classified based on severity:

Low: Minor internal exposure, no critical impact
Medium: Limited data exposure, manageable impact
High: Significant breach involving confidential or personal data
Critical: Large-scale breach with legal, financial, or reputational risk
Assessment parameters:

Type and sensitivity of data affected
Number of records impacted
Potential business and legal impact
ISRPL ensures quick containment to prevent further damage:

Isolation of affected systems or networks
Disabling compromised user accounts
Retrieval of leaked or exposed physical documents (if possible)
Blocking unauthorized access channels
Objective:
Prevent further data leakage or system compromise
A detailed investigation is conducted to determine:

Source and cause of the breach
Systems or processes affected
Extent of data exposure
Methods used:

System log analysis
Forensic investigation (if required)
Interviews with involved personnel
Depending on severity, ISRPL ensures appropriate escalation:

Internal escalation to:
Senior Management
Compliance / Legal team
External notification (if required):
Regulatory authorities
Affected stakeholders or clients
Note:
Notifications are made in accordance with applicable laws and contractual obligations
ISRPL initiates recovery actions to restore normal operations:

Restoration of systems from secure backups
Revalidation of system integrity
Reinstatement of access controls
Post-recovery checks:

Ensure no residual vulnerabilities exist
Validate system functionality and data accuracy
Based on findings, ISRPL implements CAPA:

Strengthening security controls
Updating policies and procedures
Fixing system vulnerabilities
Enhancing monitoring mechanisms

blocks.text: All incidents are documented in detail:

Incident description and timeline
Root cause and impact analysis
Actions taken (containment, recovery, CAPA)

To outline the formalized process for seeking, reviewing, granting, recording, and monitoring specific approvals within ISRPL, ensuring all requests are managed transparently, ethically, and in accordance with company policy and applicable laws.

This SOP applies to all employees, directors, and business associates of ISRPL who require specific approval for activities, transactions, or exceptions to policies and involves functional heads, management, and designated authorities.

rows.definition: Authorization granted for particular transactions, activities, or exceptions which are outside the routine delegation or require higher-level endorsement.
Individual(s) or committee designated to grant approvals as per the company's delegation matrix.
Authentic documentation of approvals granted, as per compliance requirements.

body.text: The requestor must submit a specific approval request in writing, detailing the nature, scope, purpose, and justification for the approval.
Requests should use the approved format (see Annexure A from Vigil Mechanism SOP) and may be digital or physical as per organizational guidelines.
All supporting documents must be attached.
The request is submitted to the appropriate authority, following the organization's escalation matrix:

Standard approvals to Functional Head;
Sensitive matters (personal data, policy exceptions, financial transactions) directly to MD/CEO/CFO/COO/Chairman/Audit Committee as applicable.
If the request involves potential conflicts of interest, it should be escalated per conflict-handling protocols.
The Competent Authority reviews the request, checks policy compliance, assesses risks, and consults relevant stakeholders as required.
Where necessary, additional information or clarifications may be sought from the requestor.
For matters involving privacy or personal data, compliance with Section 43A of the IT Act and the company's Privacy Policy is mandatory.
Decisions will be documented:

Approval shall include conditions, duration, and scope.
Rejection shall provide reason(s).
The decision is formally communicated to the requestor.

blocks.text: All requests and decisions are recorded and securely maintained by HR/Admin/Legal as per the company's record retention policy.
Records must include request details, authority, decision, and supporting documentation.
Records of specific approvals are reviewed quarterly by the Audit Committee and relevant Management for compliance and process improvement.
Any changes or amendments to the approval process will be updated in the SOP and communicated organization-wide.
Disputes or concerns regarding approvals may be addressed to the Grievance Officer (as per the Privacy SOP) or escalated directly to the Chairman of Audit Committee in sensitive cases.
Protective disclosure forms and confidentiality protocols must be followed.
All information pertaining to specific approval requests is considered confidential and handled as per company's Privacy Policy and Vigil Mechanism.
Whistleblowers or parties raising legitimate concerns are protected from victimization.

Monitoring of network traffic for suspicious activity
